name: Heliopause + Interstellar Space
story: The boundary where the Sun's solar wind loses its battle against the interstellar medium — roughly 120 AU out. Inside lies the heliosphere, a bubble of charged solar particles streaming outward at hundreds of km/s. Beyond it: the cold, dense gas and cosmic rays of the galaxy itself. The Voyager probes are the only artefacts humanity has ever placed across this boundary — Voyager 1 crossed in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018. Both still transmit data, faintly, from interstellar space.
comparison: About 4× farther than Neptune. A signal from Voyager 1 takes ~22 hours to reach Earth. The probes will not encounter another star for 40,000+ years (Voyager 1 will pass within 1.6 light-years of Gliese 445 in ~40,000 years).

firsts.label: Voyager 1 crosses the heliopause — first artefact in interstellar space (USA)
